clue.text: Brenda's outside, given very little air in site of Oktoberfest

indicators.note: the outside of the name Brenda means just its first and last letters

parts.note: an aria is a short song or air in an opera

explanation.surface: A woman named Brenda sits outdoors at the beer festival, short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich's Oktoberfest is held in the German state that bears this name, so it is a geographical example.

clue.text: Posh element round refuse to shun rich uncle, primarily

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol of the element tin
a round thing, a ring, is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: to shun is to avoid, so these letters are kept out of the word for refuse

parts.note: refuse means rubbish, waste

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letters of rich and uncle

explanation.surface: A snooty set refuses to have anything to do with a wealthy relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shun' drops R and U, the first letters of rich and uncle (picked by 'primarily'), from RUBBISH, leaving BBISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobbish people affect superiority, which is the colloquial sense of posh as an adjective.

clue.text: Dandy's tie making a statement

indicators.note: making a statement means speaking out, so the word is taken as it is said

parts.note: a bow is a tie, as in a bow tie or a knot with loops

explanation.surface: A dandy's flamboyant neckwear is meant to be a fashion statement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'making a statement' means showy; here it signals the spoken form of BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau in older usage is a man fussy about his clothes, a synonym for a fop.

clue.text: After time, gardener may pull up these clothing items

indicators.note: the plants follow the letter for time, so they come after it

parts.note: weeds are what a gardener uproots

explanation.surface: After a while, a gardener might yank up certain garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweeds are suits or garments made of a rough woollen cloth, so they are examples of clothing.

clue.text: Academic briefly replacing priest heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the letters run upwards, so they are read backwards

parts.note: for can mean in place of, as in swapping one thing for another

explanation.surface: A shortened academic title takes over from a clergyman who is travelling north.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the clipped informal form of professor, hence the 'briefly' in the definition.

clue.text: American touring definitely close to tiger sharks?

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the American letters surround the rest

parts.note: US is short for the United States, so American
sure means definitely, as in 'sure, I'll come'

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of tiger

explanation.surface: An American traveller is certain they got near to tiger sharks.
explanation.definitionFit: Loan sharks lend money at exorbitant interest, which is what these moneylenders do; the question mark flags the figurative sense.

clue.text: Activity of driver after stoppin' for cake

indicators.note: the dropped g of stoppin' shows the same clipping is done: the final letter is lost

parts.note: parking a car is something a driver does

explanation.surface: A motorist pulls over to buy a cake, talking in a lazy drawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoppin'' is both a parking pun and an example of dropping the final G, which is what happens to PARKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a dense gingerbread made with oatmeal and treacle, a traditional cake from Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Mystic's spirit, over two books, followed by celebrity type

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above what follows
followed by means the next piece comes after

parts.note: in Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spiritual double
B is an abbreviation for book, so two books are two Bs
an A-list person is a top celebrity

explanation.surface: A mystic's ghost hovers above two volumes, chased by a famous sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Kabbalah, the Jewish esoteric tradition, is a kind of mystic.

clue.text: Newsman watches triple jumper

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a newsman
wards as a verb means guards or watches over

explanation.surface: A newsreader observes a triple jump athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newsman' seems to point at the BBC presenter Huw Edwards, but it only gives ED; the definition is Jonathan Edwards, the British triple-jump world-record holder.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Edwards is the British athlete who still holds the world record in the triple jump.

clue.text: Preserve black part of doorway?

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to keep a dark section of a door frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is one of the upright side posts of a door or window frame.

clue.text: Aussie maybe in olden days describing Wallabies' game

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round, so the old-days letters encircle the game

parts.note: BCE, before the common era, marks ancient dates
the Wallabies are Australia's rugby union team, and RU stands for rugby union

explanation.surface: An Australian, long ago, explains how the national rugby team plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruce is the stock name for a typical Australian man in British humour, so this is an example.

clue.text: Crossing beneficial to little daughter

parts.note: for means in favour of or good for
D is the short form of daughter

explanation.surface: A road junction that is helpful to a small girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A ford is a shallow place where a river can be crossed.

clue.text: Artist's agent rejected one duty in five

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for the number

parts.note: the number word itself is cut open

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a duty is a tax

explanation.surface: A painter's representative turns down a fee, one fifth of a levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's agent' reads like a person who represents painters, but it means a substance; 'rejected' reverses one plus duty, and 'in' sets that inside the number word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixative is sprayed on drawings to fix them, an agent or substance used by artists.

clue.text: Order policemen, in extremes of temperature, to retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the whole is read in reverse
in means the police letters go inside
extremes of means the outermost letters of temperature

parts.note: the CID is the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Police officers are ordered to withdraw from extreme heat and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is Britain's detective branch; 'in' and 'extremes of' build the container, and 'to retreat' turns the whole thing round.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or command issued by authority.

clue.text: Royal house pioneer owns open to all

indicators.note: owns means holds, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: to pioneer something is to start it
U is the British film rating for films anyone may see

explanation.surface: A trailblazer's house is a royal one open to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stuarts were the dynasty that ruled Scotland and later England in the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Vagrant is snugly embracing area like the back end of a bus

definitions.text: like the back end of a bus

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the shuffled letters surround the abbreviation
vagrant means wandering, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A tramp is cosily hugging someone unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vagrant' rearranges IS SNUGLY, and 'embracing' wraps those letters round A.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as ugly as the back end of a bus' describes someone very unattractive.

clue.text: Bird almost ready to face strong wind

parts.note: nigh means nearly, almost
tin and ready are both slang for cash
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A bird nearly prepared to fly into a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is not an adjective here but money slang, as in readies.
explanation.definitionFit: This songbird is famous for its rich song heard at night.

clue.text: Teeth become more noticeable after such confectionery?

definitions.text: Teeth become more noticeable after such confectionery?

parts.words: Teeth become more noticeable after such confectionery?
parts.note: read as gums drop, receding gums make teeth look longer, while the whole names chewy sweets

explanation.surface: Eating certain sweets makes your teeth stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: These are chewy sugar-coated jelly sweets, a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: Advance towards a landing-place, mostly underwater

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a quay is a landing place for boats

explanation.surface: A boat edges towards a jetty, mostly beneath the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub-aqua describes sports such as diving that take place beneath the water.

clue.text: Prejudiced British one offering encouragement to Edward

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
go! is a shout of encouragement
Ted is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: A biased Briton cheers on a man called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigoted people hold intolerant, unreasoning opinions, so they are biased.

clue.text: Jurgen's out, close to limit in old car

parts.note: aus is the German for out, and Jurgen is a typical German name

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of limit

explanation.surface: A German man called Jurgen is out of the old car, nearly at the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: Jurgen signals German, so 'out' is translated into that language.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin was a British car maker, so an Austin is a vintage motor.

clue.text: Leather coat from Nassau obtained with US money

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outer layer, its first and last letters

parts.note: a buck is a US dollar

explanation.surface: A leather jacket bought in the Bahamas capital paid for in dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubuck is a cowhide leather buffed to a velvety finish.

clue.text: Lyricist Rice heard sudden dread of a drum

indicators.note: heard means the name is taken as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: Tim Rice wrote the lyrics for Evita and other musicals
panic is sudden fear

explanation.surface: Tim Rice was heard to be terrified of a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tympanic is the adjective from tympanum, the eardrum or a drum.

clue.text: Some retired villagers showing bitterness

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the letters run in reverse
some means a part of the word villagers is taken

explanation.surface: A few pensioners in the village are resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes LLAG from villagers and 'retired' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gall is resentment or bile, a synonym for bitterness.

clue.text: Learning lives of Roman Emperors (earliest only)

indicators.note: earliest only means just the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: Scholarship about the early biographies of Roman emperors.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is traditional knowledge or learning.

clue.text: Regulars inside keen to plug pub job

indicators.note: to plug means to fill a hole, so these letters go into the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: regular letters from inside the word keen means every other letter

explanation.surface: Regular drinkers in a pub are eager to promote the place's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regulars inside' takes K and E from keen (first and third letters).
explanation.definitionFit: A baker is someone whose trade is making bread, an occupation.

clue.text: One's flown east with Christopher

parts.note: Kit is a nickname for Christopher

explanation.surface: A man named Christopher has flown east.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a toy on a string that is flown in the wind.

clue.text: Weather condition broadcast around noon

indicators.note: around means the scattering word goes round the letter for noon

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it, scattering it widely

explanation.surface: A weather report is aired at about midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a radio forecast but means scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is a kind of precipitation, so an example of weather.

clue.text: Truth circulated about financial centre in European city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the postcode
circulated means sent round, so the letters move about

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial centre

explanation.surface: The facts were spread around a European banking hub.
explanation.walkthrough: London's financial district, the City, has EC postcodes; 'circulated' shuffles the first word, and 'about' wraps it round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Tank once used to attack unknown ruler

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, attack in a review
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A tank was formerly used to assault an unidentified monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panzer was a German armoured fighting vehicle of the Second World War.
